title: Port a depot staffing script

blocks.text: A storm-response depot plans its crews with an old pywraplp script, `legacy_plan(data)` in `staffing.py`. The planning service is moving to MathOpt. Write `mathopt_plan(data)`: the same model in MathOpt, solved by SCIP, returning what `legacy_plan` returns: `("OPTIMAL", cost, {variable name: value})`, or `(reason name, None, None)` when the solve is not optimal (use `result.termination.reason.name`).
Read the legacy function first; it is the specification. Its model, with $`K`$ the crew kinds:

$`n_k`$ is the number of crews of kind $`k`$, each covering $`h_k`$ hours at cost $`c_k`$, between the union minimum $`m_k`$ and the most available $`\bar n_k`$; $`o`$ is overtime hours at rate $`r`$ per hour, at most $`\bar o`$; the depot needs between $`L`$ and $`U`$ hours covered. Keep the variable names the old script uses (`crews_<kind>`, `overtime`).
The tests run both functions on several depots and check that they agree on the status, the cost and the variables reported. About fifteen lines.

"""Run executes this file. Change the calls and see what prints. Submit grades."""
import logging

# Turn the logger up, so the `log.debug` lines of your code show under the printed lines.
logging.basicConfig(level=logging.DEBUG, format="%(levelname)s %(message)s")

from staffing import legacy_plan, mathopt_plan

# kind -> (hours a crew covers, cost of a crew, most crews, union minimum)
yard = {"crews": {"dock": (35, 25, 5, 1), "crane": (45, 40, 3, 0), "temp": (20, 18, 6, 0)},
        "need_low": 150, "need_high": 190, "overtime_max": 30, "overtime_rate": 0.8}
print("legacy:", legacy_plan(yard))
print("mathopt:", mathopt_plan(yard))
tight = dict(yard, crews=dict(yard["crews"], dock=(35, 25, 5, 4), crane=(45, 40, 3, 2)))
print("legacy, minimums dock 4, crane 2:", legacy_plan(tight))
print("mathopt, minimums dock 4, crane 2:", mathopt_plan(tight))

cases.says: on the base depot the port reaches the legacy cost and reports the same variables
with overtime dearer than crews, the port still keeps overtime at or above zero
where a fraction of a crew would be cheaper, the port still hires whole crews
a crew kind's minimum, set with SetBounds in the old script, holds in the port
the cover row's upper bound holds, so a depot whose minimums exceed it is infeasible in both

origin.section: Every pywraplp Call Has a MathOpt Counterpart

concepts: each pywraplp call, bound and status has a MathOpt counterpart, and bounds left out of a MathOpt variable are infinite
